question: What is the primary goal of family planning counselling?

options.A: Ensuring every client chooses modern barrier methods
options.B: Reducing the overall birth rate in rural communities
options.C: Convincing every client to use permanent surgical methods
options.D: Helping clients make free and informed reproductive choices

explanation: Counselling empowers clients to make voluntary decisions about their own families rather than forcing a specific choice upon them. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h1)

question: What is a likely result of poor family planning counselling?

options.A: Higher rates of natural family planning use
options.B: Better adherence to daily pill schedules
options.C: Early discontinuation of the contraceptive method
options.D: Increased long-term loyalty to clinic staff

explanation: When clients do not fully understand what to expect or how to use their method, they tend to stop using it quickly. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h1)

question: What does the principle of autonomy mean in family planning?

options.A: Clinics must provide free medications to every community member
options.B: Husbands must approve all medical treatments before they begin
options.C: Clients have the right to make their own choices without coercion
options.D: Nurses must choose the safest contraceptive for young clients

explanation: Autonomy protects the client's right to self-determination in their personal reproductive healthcare decisions. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h2)

question: Why is strict confidentiality vital during family planning sessions?

options.A: It builds trust and encourages clients to seek needed care safely
options.B: It guarantees that the government will fund the clinic supplies
options.C: It prevents hospital administrators from auditing patient records
options.D: It stops family members from asking about the client's health

explanation: Clients need assurance that their private reproductive health details will not be shared openly in the community. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h2)

question: What does the letter 'T' stand for in the GATHER counselling model?
explanation: In GATHER, 'Tell' refers to sharing relevant and balanced information about available contraceptive methods with the client. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h3)

question: A nurse is finishing a counselling session by booking a follow-up date and inviting the client back if problems arise. Which GATHER step is this?
explanation: The 'Return' step focuses on planning for future visits, follow-up care, and open-door re-evaluations. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h3)

question: Why are open-ended questions preferred during reproductive health counselling?

options.A: They shorten the time needed to complete patient registration
options.B: They encourage clients to share their thoughts and concerns fully
options.C: They ensure the nurse makes all the final medical decisions
options.D: They prevent clients from asking complicated medical questions

explanation: Open-ended questions allow clients to express their true feelings and personal stories rather than giving a simple one-word answer. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of an open-ended question?

options.A: Are you finished having children with your husband?
options.B: Do you want to use pills or injections today?
options.C: What worries you most about using family planning methods?
options.D: Have you ever experienced high blood pressure before?

explanation: This question cannot be answered with a simple yes or no, prompting the client to elaborate on their specific fears. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h4)

question: What standardized tool do nurses use to check if a contraceptive method is safe for a specific medical condition?
explanation: The WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria guide providers on the safety of various contraceptives for clients with specific health conditions. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h5)

question: A client with severe high blood pressure requests a combined oral contraceptive pill. What is the most appropriate nursing action based on safety guidelines?

options.A: Dispense the pills immediately to respect her personal autonomy and choice
options.B: Double the normal starting dose to make sure the pills work effectively
options.C: Tell her to stop checking her blood pressure while taking the hormonal medication
options.D: Suggest an alternative safe method because combined pills pose high cardiovascular risks here

explanation: Combined oral contraceptives can worsen hypertension and increase stroke risks, making them medically restricted for this client. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h5)

question: How should a nurse present different contraceptive choices to a client?

options.A: By strongly recommending the most expensive brand in the clinic
options.B: Objectively, sharing both benefits and drawbacks of each method
options.C: By focusing only on permanent surgical options for parity
options.D: By hiding common side effects so the client does not get scared

explanation: Balanced presentation ensures the client makes a truly informed decision based on complete facts. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h6)

question: Which of the following is classified as a long-acting reversible contraceptive?
explanation: Implants provide continuous protection for several years while remaining fully reversible upon removal. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h6)

question: What is the best way to handle a client who expresses fear that an injectable contraceptive causes permanent barrenness?

options.A: Refuse to provide any family planning services to uneducated clients
options.B: Laugh at the misconception so they realize how silly it sounds
options.C: Tell them they must accept whatever side effects happen without complaining
options.D: Listen patiently, validate their worry, and provide factual reassurance

explanation: Respectful dialogue and clear facts help dispel deep-seated cultural myths without shaming the client. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended nursing approach when correcting common contraceptive myths?

options.B: Insulting the client for believing rumors
options.C: Providing clear and accurate health facts

explanation: Insulting clients creates a hostile environment and drives them away from formal healthcare facilities. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h7)

question: Why is spousal communication often encouraged in Nigerian family planning counselling?

options.A: Partner support helps improve long-term contraceptive adherence
options.B: Nigerian law prohibits women from buying drugs independently
options.C: Men are the only ones who experience contraceptive side effects
options.D: Husbands must legally sign all medical forms in public hospitals

explanation: When partners understand and support the chosen method, the client faces less household conflict and continues use more successfully. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h8)

question: What common barrier often affects contraceptive uptake in resource-constrained Nigerian communities?

options.A: Universal preference for large families exceeding ten children
options.B: Financial constraints and out-of-pocket supply costs
options.C: An absolute lack of any modern contraceptive methods globally
options.D: Laws that ban nurses from discussing birth control openly

explanation: Poverty and high out-of-pocket costs make access difficult, making knowledge of subsidized options vital for nurses. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h8)
